rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Matching dimensions does not fix a factor of 2.  ·  A degree Celsius interval is a temperature difference. A formula that needs kelvin must be given kelvin.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: [g] = [L T^-2], the same as acceleration.  ·  A spring constant k in F = kx has dimensions of force over length.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: The dimension of a quantity records which base quantities it contains and to what power. In mechanics the symbols are M for mass, L for length and T for time. The dimensional formula of speed is [L T^-1].  ·  Force is mass times acceleration, and acceleration is length over time squared, so [F] = [M L T^-2]. Work and energy are force times distance, so [W] = [M L^2 T^-2]. Power is energy over time, so [P] = [M L^2 T^-3].

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: sin(x) is legal only when x is dimensionless.  ·  Energy and torque share [M L^2 T^-2], so dimensions cannot tell them apart.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: An equation can be right only if every term has the same dimensions. This is a necessary check, not a proof that the equation is the correct physical law. A missing numerical factor such as 1/2 is invisible to dimensions.  ·  Angles in radians, strains, and coefficients that are pure ratios have dimension 1. They may be arguments of a sine or an exponential. A dimensioned quantity may not sit alone inside a sine.  ·  The dimensional formula is written in square brackets. [v] = [M^0 L T^-1] says mass does not appear. Leaving out a zero power is allowed when the quantity is absent.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Changing the unit, from metres to centimetres, does not change the dimension. Dimensions and units are related, but they are not the same statement.
